fields.hint: Picture `git log` walking from the newest entry back to older ones, and ask what it follows.
fields.explanation: Each commit stores the id of the commit it was built on (two or more for a merge; the very first commit has none), so the history is a graph Git can walk backwards. That is what makes `git log`, diffs between any two commits and merges possible; a zip archive or a single file would hold one state with no link from one version to the next, and Git keeps its objects as files under `.git`, not in a database table.

notes: Root-commit exception added so every claim in the explanation holds.

fields.explanation: `git switch feature` moves HEAD to the `feature` branch and updates the working tree to match it. Switch is the modern half of the old `git checkout`, whose other half — restoring files — is now `git restore`, and creating a brand-new branch as you switch needs `-c`.

fields.explanation: Merging one branch into another produces a commit with two parents — the previous tip of the branch you were on and the tip of the branch you merged — which is what keeps both histories reachable afterwards. One parent means an ordinary commit or a fast-forward, where no merge commit is created at all; more than two parents only comes from an octopus merge, where you name several branches in one `git merge` command.

fields.hint: You commit locally and `git status` says 'ahead 1'. Ask what it compared your branch with.
fields.explanation: `origin/main` is a remote-tracking ref recording where `main` was on `origin` the last time Git contacted it — at clone, fetch, pull or push. It does not move while you commit locally, which is exactly how `git status` can tell you that you are 'ahead 1'; it catches up only when Git next talks to the remote.

problems: hint ('it only changes when Git talks to the remote') states the rule the item tests
explanation contradicted itself: it listed push as one of the moments the ref updates, then said only a fetch or pull brings it up to date
evidence: run: after push, main=4d70c4b and origin/main=4d70c4b; after one local commit, main=10b0eae while origin/main stayed 4d70c4b; git status -sb -> '## main...origin/main [ahead 1]'
run: after pushing again, origin/main=10b0eae (a push does update the remote-tracking ref)
notes: Key and options unchanged; the fix removes the internal contradiction about what updates the ref.
